utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning to you call. We're going to make two oral rulings, the first of which concerns the accused's oral request regarding the meeting with his expert witness in the holding cell. Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber has consulted with various organs of the registry concerning your request to have your Defence expert meet with you in the holding cell during breaks. The Registry has agreed that it can accommodate this request on the understanding that it is only in those cases where the Chamber has issued a decision granting a request from you that a specific Defence expert should be permitted in the courtroom during the testimony of a certain Prosecution witness or witnesses, that such authorisation is given. Furthermore, you must make a request through the pro se officer that you wish to avail yourself of this possibility in each case at least two working days in advance of the relevant Defence expert being present so that his or her name can be added to the list of persons permitted entry to the holding cells with you. This is to ensure that security has at least 24 hours notice of any addition to that list. In addition, your Defence expert must be accompanied at all times when he or she is in the holding cell by one of your privileged legal associates. At any time, only two people, in addition to yourself, i.e., three in total, will be permitted in the holding cell. Should you have any questions or require further clarification about the procedure to be followed, please address those questions to the Registry through the pro se officer. On a related note, I have been asked to advise you that due to an oversight yesterday, Dr. Subotic was permitted to sit directly beside you in the courtroom. As you know, this is not the normal procedure, and your assigned legal -- associate sits at a certain distance from you. In future, whenever Dr. Subotic or other permitted Defence experts are in the courtroom, they will sit in the usual place beside your assigned associates. Again, any questions in this regard should be addressed to the Registry. Second ruling concerns the Prosecution motion for leave to amend it's Rule 65 ter exhibit list regarding authentication of the Mladic notebook. On 17th August 2010, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting leave from the Chamber to amend it's Rule 65 ter exhibit list by adding to it three reports which it wishes to use with the next witness, Mr. Tomasz Blaszczyk. The reports were authored by the Serbian authorities, and they describe the date, the time, and the locations of the seizures of items from the Belgrade residence of Bosiljka Mladic, wife of General Ratko Mladic, during searches conducted by the authorities at the end of 2009 and early 2010. The reports also provide inventories of the items seized. The accused filed his response to the Prosecution's request on 18th of August. He does not oppose the addition of -- addition of two of these three reports but does oppose the addition of the third. He notes that the third report with Rule 65 ter number 22939 is a 440-page document which "purports to describe the contents of approximately 100 recordings" disclosed to him on 4th of August, 2010, and in respect of which he has not had adequate time to review. In his motion on the suspension of proceedings, the accused indicates his belief that these recordings may contain recordings of some of the meetings described in notebooks, ostensibly written by Ratko Mladic, which were also seized by Serbian authorities from Mrs. Mladic's residence. As is clear from Prosecution's motion, as well as its notification for him, Tomasz Blaszczyk is being brought by the Prosecution at this stage to provide evidence going to authenticity of the notebooks and the three reports are to be used in this context only. As such, the content of the recordings noted in the third report will not be at issue. In this regard, while Tomasz Blaszczyk may testify that certain documents and videos corroborate the information contained in the notebooks, it appears from the witness's notification that these items do not include the recordings referred to in the third report. Since Tomasz Blaszczyk's evidence will not deal with the recordings, the Chamber is satisfied that it is not necessary for the accused to have reviewed them before the addition of the report to the Prosecution's exhibit list and that he will not suffer prejudice by not having yet reviewed them. The Chamber considers that in providing information as to the circumstances in which the notebook was seized, including the dates of the seizures and the other material taken with notebooks, the three reports are prima facie relevant to the present case. The Chamber has also considered when the three reports were disclosed to the accused and their subject matter. Therefore, it is satisfied that the Prosecution has shown good cause for its request and that the three reports are of sufficient importance to justify their late addition to its exhibit list. As such, the Chamber finds that it is in the interest of justice to grant the Prosecution leave to add the three reports to its exhibit list. However, as the Chamber has stated previously, the addition of documents to an exhibit list and their admission into evidence are different matters. It is not clear to the Chamber at this moment how the three reports assist with the authentication of the notebooks. Before exploring this further, the Chamber would like to hear from Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Karadzic, as you know, the Prosecution is of the view that the notebooks were authored by Ratko Mladic. Do you accept this or do you intend to challenge the authenticity of the notebooks?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I can answer that on Dr. Karadzic's behalf. We're putting the Prosecution to its proof to see whether or not they can prove or it's established that -- through the testimony of this next witness with -- that these notebooks were authored by General Mladic. After the testimony of the witness and the cross-examination of Dr. Karadzic, we'll give you a clear answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then I would like to ask the Prosecution or hear from the Prosecution as to how these three reports and particularly the third report with the Rule 65 ter number 22939 will assist in establishing the authenticity of the notebooks.

I intend to use the other two -- the other inventory reports. The way that I believe they may be helpful, and I have a handout which shows this, is that -- is simply for chain of custody, that we're able to establish that the notebooks that we now have in our evidence unit appear on the inventory list as the notebooks which were taken in the two searches from General Mladic's wife's apartment. So these contemporaneous inventory lists created by the Serbian MUP show that on the dates of the searches these items were taken from that particular residence and that they are the same items which were ultimately received by the OTP. So it is mainly a matter of chain of custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, but it happened in the search conducted on 23 February 2010, and she paginated all the notebooks, and he -- she signed also -- she confirmed the number of the pages of each notebook at the end of the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 22840, please, in e-court. All right. If we can just keep that first page up for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While we're on it, Mr. Blaszczyk, can you tell us who put on the -- where that Post-It note the with the "40" comes from?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The officer of Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. That was there when we received the item?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct. How the -- how the evidence was marked by the Serbian MUP and we receive in this shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we now go to the very last page, 405. Simply showing the back cover of the notebook. And -- that's right. Could we leave that on the English. That's page 400 of the English we're looking at. Could we now look at page 404 of the B/C/S, original.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, we see on the screen there, is that the certification by Bosiljka Mladic that you were just explaining to us?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct. This is certification and confirmation of Bosiljka Mladic that this book contains 396 pages, handwritten pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you receive any information of why these books were marked in this way, these notebooks, by General Mladic's wife?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I did receive this information yesterday. According to information we received from Serbs, Bosiljka Mladic considers this notebooks as very important notebooks, and this is why she insisted to paginate these notebooks and confirm the number of the pages at the end of each notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'm done with that exhibit. And again very briefly, if you could explain to the Trial Chamber just a quick chronology of how the OTP came into possession of these original notebooks from the December search -- from the 2010 search, excuse me?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The notebooks, this material was seized during the search of the house of Bosiljka Mladic in 23 February 2010, and to one month later the ICTY received also scanned version of -- of the seized material on the hard drive, and the original material was handed over to our ICTY field office, to our investigator from ICTY field office in Belgrade on 27 April 2010, and later on I arrived to Belgrade and together with this investigator I transported entire material to -- to The Hague. It was done between 10 and 11 May 2010, and on 11 May I submitted entire material to our evidence unit here in The Hague. Since the material was handed over by Serbian authority to our investigator from the field office, this material was accessible only to our investigator from the field office. Nobody else had access to this material. When I arrived to the Belgrade together with my colleague from the field office we counted -- we checked again the inventory list of the Serbian MUP. We unpacked the boxes received by them. We counted the seized items, and we packed it again, and the following day we transported it to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And now we're not going to discuss it today, but just to be clear for the record, there were many other items seized as well during the 23 February 2010 search?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Is correct. Is correct. There were many items, not only notebook but also other material.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, discussing the notebooks which were -- that we're talking about now from the second search in 2010, after the OTP received the scans of the notebook from the MUP, did you take any steps, conduct any interviews to authenticate who had written these notebooks?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. On 26, 27 April 2010, we interviewed General Manojlo Milovanovic, and we showed him -- we produced to him the copy, of course, the copy of -- the scanned version of the seized notebooks, 17 notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just briefly for the record, who is General Milovanovic? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: General Manojlo Milovanovic, this was Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of Army of Republika Srpska and deputy commander of the Army of Republika Srpska. He was directly subordinated to General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long was -- during the war was General Milovanovic subordinated directly to General Ratko Mladic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: According to General Milovanovic, he was -- he know -- he knew General Mladic since 1981 even, I think, but he was directly subordinated to him, he was his deputy, since the beginning of the war, since May 2002, since the Republika Srpska Army was created, till the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I think that's May 1992.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: 1992. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And was General -- what determination did -- was General Milovanovic able to make when he reviewed the scanned notebooks?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: As I said, General -- General Milovanovic, while he was here in The Hague, he was -- he got from us the scanned version of all 17 notebooks, and he had time to review entire scanned version of these notebooks, and he confirm that in chart, which we have in his statement, he confirmed that most of the pages are the pages handwritten by General Ratko Mladic. General Milovanovic work with General Ratko Mladic on daily basis. He participated most of the meetings from which General Mladic was present while he was writing down the notes, and he is very familiar, as he said, with his handwritings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you met General Milovanovic in April of this year, did you discuss at all the five notebooks from the earlier search, from 2008? Did he comments on those and who had written those notebooks?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I remember when I met General Milovanovic here in The Hague on 25th, 20 -- 26th, 27th, I think, April, I brought these five notebooks from the first seizure with me to the interviewing room, and General Milovanovic had opportunity to see these notebooks, but he confirmed that he reviewed these notebooks during the meeting with my investigator colleague in Banja Luka one year before. It was -- I believe it was June 2009. And he confirmed that he -- he had opportunity to see these notebooks in -- the same notebooks I brought to our interviewing room, and -- and he confirmed that this is handwritten notebooks, handwritten text, done by General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, those five notebooks are 65 ter numbers 13416, 19023, 19022, 13452, and 13450 from the first search.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you stated that General Milovanovic stated he recognised in the scans that most of the handwriting was of General Mladic. Was the other handwriting -- what was that? Was that letters, other documents that had been inside the covers of the notebooks?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Exactly. They were another document just slipped inside the notebooks, but at that time we were in possession only on -- of the scanned version of -- of these documents. In fact, we didn't know exactly what is -- what is the part the page of the notebook, what the slipped piece of paper or page to the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to now --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could ask the Defence to give me back a piece of evidence which I gave to them this morning to inspect. If the usher could help me. If we could hand that to the witness, please. And for the record, the witness has been given the notebook with ERN 13452. Can you just tell us quickly which -- what -- what that is before you and which search that was taken in?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is ERN 06490326, I think, starting, and this is notebook seized by Serbian MUP in the search from 4 December 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's an original copy?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, this is original notebook seized at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay of the I'd like to show a video now, please. That's 40241A.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "Colonel Karremans: Our own medicines are almost zero --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we stop, please, for one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I have no broadcast of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could start it again for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "Colonel Karremans: Our own medicines are almost zero."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we stop please now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think you're very familiar with this video, Mr. Blaszczyk. Can you just tell us -- we're only playing a short one-minute clip, but where is this video taken from and who do we see here in the first frame?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is a video recorded during the meeting of General Mladic and other officers of Army of Republika Srpska with DutchBat commander and Muslim representative in Bratunac. This meeting took place on 11 July 1995. It was the second meeting in Bratunac, in Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. And we're at 1:24:03. Could you tell us who is in screen here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Right now on the screen I see the interpreter who is translating the words of Colonel Karremans, the commander of the DutchBat from Potocari. He's on the right side, the man with uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Could we continue playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "Colonel Karremans: The only thing what I can do is the two surgery teams. They have done it in the afternoon and tonight is a big surgery, but that's only for a couple of persons and then the medicines for those special surgery is left as well."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we stop for one moment, please. We're at 1:24:30.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, as we look at the screen there's a man in uniform with glasses taking notes. Can you tell us who that person is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This is Colonel Radoslav Jankovic, the head of intelligence service of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Continue playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "Colonel Karremans: If I may say so, sir..."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Please stop here at 1:24:41.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Quite obvious, but who -- who do we see in the clip we just saw some footage of, the man on the left writing in a notebook?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: On this footage, on this still we see General Ratko Mladic taking notes in his notebooks. I believe this is this notebook, the entry from this notebook corroborate to this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we continue just playing to the end of this short clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "Colonel Karremans: I think that the evacuation of the wounded could be the second thing to be organised."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And we stop here at 1:24:55 where General Mladic has just finished taking notes on the bottom right hand page of the notebook he's writing in as Colonel Karremans has been explaining that an evacuation needs to be carried out. Could we now have 65 ter 13452 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the time, can the Chamber take a look at the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed. We can proceed in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. There we see the cover on the left. And can we go to page 224 in the English and page 227 in the B/C/S. I'm just waiting for the B/C/S to come up. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, we see there that this is an entry for 11 July, Bratunac, meeting with the UN commander in Srebrenica and representatives of the Muslim side, Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans, and it's correct, Mr. Blaszczyk, that General Mladic has written here "Colonel Jankovic took the minutes." Is that the same Jankovic we saw writing notes in the video just a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, this is the same Jankovic, Colonel Radoslav Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page, please in both the English and the B/C/S. We need the next page in the English. All right. Now, Your Honours, the English version corresponds to the B/C/S. That's why there's space at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But we can see here, Mr. Blaszczyk, is that right, that on the bottom right-hand corner of the notebook Mr. -- General Mladic has written notes saying "I have two surgical teams. They performed a few serious operations and used up the medicines. Evacuation of the wounded to be carried out"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct, and this corroborated by the video we just saw a few seconds ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if you review the video, I won't play it again for time, but the statements that General Karremans is making on that video being translated to General Mladic, it corresponds exactly to his writing at that time in the same portion of the notebook. Could I have 65 ter 90185, please. That's a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, that is not bad, but not as clear as in the hard copy if anybody would like to see it. Now, could you tell us why -- well, who prepared this photograph?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I selected this photograph, but was prepared by our video assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Why did you select this photograph? What did you -- why did you choose this image?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I believe this is the best view of the notebook used by General Ratko Mladic and is visible on the photos -- I think on the printed version is much better -- is better quality at least, that we can see water mark in the shape of the pen which is in original notebook used by -- which we have in our possession. Is exactly the same one. If we look the original and we see this water mark, this -- this water mark is visible on this clip in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if I could now ask to put on the ELMO just so that it's very clear the -- I'm putting up pages 06490552 and 06490553 of the original notebook which is the first page of General Mladic's, excuse me, notes on the 11 July Fontana meeting. If we can pan out a little bit. If we could bring it out a bit so that we can see both full pages. So in the photograph which we just saw, Mr. Blaszczyk, you selected that because one can see that watermarks of the two pens on the top of the two pages; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. And also in the previous clip we played just few seconds ago we see that General Mladic is writing down the notes regarding these two surgical teams and the wounded person, and he's writing this information on -- on the right-hand side page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I ask Your Honours to tender 40241A, the video-clip, as well as the photo still which is 90185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it that video 40241A should be the -- an excerpt from the entire video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. That's just -- if I'm correct, that's just the -- that is the number which sub -- 65 ter number we have assigned to that expert which is from the larger video which is on our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the time-frame you referred to, such as 1:24:03, seems to be the time-frame in the entire video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So when you tender you will excerpt only those parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Just that part, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then the time-frame you referred to will not match with the video you will tender, but that -- given the time period is very short, I don't see any problem. Do you have any objection, Mr. Robinson? So we'll admit them both, the video as well as the still taken from the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video extract with 65 ter number 40241A will be Exhibit P1458, and 65 ter 90185 will be Exhibit P1459.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to show another very short video-clip. This has been assigned our number 40032A.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we stop for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Blaszczyk, the date and location of this video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This video was recorded in Boksanica. This is place near Zepa. On 19 July 1995. And this is meeting between representative of the Zepa population and the members of the Army of Republika Srpska and Ukrainian Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We had stopped at -- well, I'll read the number 12:29:3, and we can't see all of them in the picture, but who is that on the right holding a notebook of some type?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Well, we see the hands of General Ratko Mladic right now holding his hands -- General Ratko Mladic holding his hands on the notebook. I believe this is this notebook. Also in this notebook we have entry from this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And could we -- I'm sorry, maybe go back because this is a very short clip. Play it again from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we stop there for one moment. 12:05. Who is that in the front, the man with the large moustache?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is Colonel Svetozar Kosoric, he's intelligence officer from the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we stop there for one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who is the man with the beard we see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is representative of the Muslim population from Zepa. His name is Benjamin Kulovac, doctor from Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we continue, please. That was at 12:41 we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who is the man on the left of the screen with the coat draped over his holders?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Another representative of the Muslim population from Zepa, Mr. Hamdija Torlak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we see there on this shot at 12:45 that General Mladic now has his notebook open. Could we just continue to the end of the clip. Oh, that is the end. Thank you. And having reviewed this video, we only saw him from the back, but can you tell us looking at the whole video any other senior VRS officer who was present, along with General Mladic and with Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. It's visible this. On this part of the video we see only the backside of General Zdravko Tolimir, but also there was present Colonel Milutinovic. He's press officer from the Army of Republika Srpska, from the high-ranking officer, another officer from the Rogatica brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And if we could now have on e-court again 65 ter 13452. That is the same original notebook which I've brought in, Your Honours. Page 228 of the English, 231 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, for our convenience if you could turn the pages of the notebook on the original so that we can see on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Very simply, Mr. Blaszczyk, here we have the entry from Wednesday, 19 July 1995, Boksanica mountain, from General Mladic's notebook. Same month as the last video we saw. Meeting with representatives of the Muslim population from Zepa. And just to confirm, Hamdija Torlak and Benjamin Kulovac. Are those the two gentleman we just saw on the video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. They were just these two gentlemens with civilian clothes we saw on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we also saw General Mladic, Generals -- the back of General Tolimir, and Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We saw General Mladic, of course, on this individual, General Tolimir, Colonel Svetozar Kosoric, and as well we saw the member of the Ukrainian battalion, Colonel Dudnjik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could tender that video-clip 40032A and, as you noted, Your Honour, the time-frames I've read apparently won't match because the clip didn't start with 0.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1460, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And one final -- sorry. Before we leave this could I show photo 90187, a photo from this meeting. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blaszczyk, having reviewed the video, can you confirm that this is a still taken from that video, just from a portion that wasn't included in the clip we saw?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is a still taken from the video we saw just before. Not entire video but part of the video, but I review entire video several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: And we see here General Tolimir, Ratko Mladic, of course; officer from logistic branch from Rogatica Brigade, Colonel Milutinovic and Colonels -- the intelligence officer, and two representatives of the Muslim population from Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And just to be very clear, which -- the individual -- which individual is General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is -- this is the man sitting next to General Mladic on his left hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could give that a number, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1461.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I'm now going into the last part. I'm sorry I've gone over the hour I anticipated. There's not much more. Some corroborating material I'll try to go through quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much more do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think less than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we better take a break right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break about 20 minutes. We'll resume at 10 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. During the break what's been passed out and you should have before you and all the parties is a hard copy of 65 ter 22943. This is the chart which was notified on the list of exhibits to be used with the witness correlating documents taken from various sources, various types of documents, to diary entries.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, do you have a copy of that chart in front of you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you confirm that you have reviewed all of the documents listed in this chart and matched them to the diary entries listed along with them in the chart?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Is correct. I reviewed all these documents mentioned here in this chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were you able to confirm that the chart accurately reflects the documents you reviewed and the diary entries?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I propose to do is now just go through a sample of these entries and matches. The first one is from 9 June 1992. If we could first have 65 ter 22840 on the screen. English pages -- starting at page 124.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And we see here now from General Mladic's notebook entry, "Pale, Tuesday 9 June 1992, at 920 hours, meeting with the Presidency of SR BH." The persons listed as present: Karadzic, Koljevic, Plavsic, Krajisnik, Djeric, Mladic, Gvero, Tolimir, and the minute taker. And then "Meeting." And could you just please read out what it says below "Meeting" next to the asterisk?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. The B/C/S page is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. It's page 123 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Below "Meeting" is written: "I briefed the state and political. The president is [indiscernible]. Leadership about situation on the front and material resources for the war."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now quickly go to D00428, which is also our 65 ter number 114, at page 1 of the English. And what we have here, thank you, are minutes of the expanded meeting of the War Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The same persons listed as present. And could you just read out the first paragraph starting with "General Mladic" after the names of the persons present listed.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "General Mladic briefed the Presidency in detail about the overall situation in the Serbian Army and gave figures on quantities of weapons, ammunition, spare parts, reserves of oil and oil products, food, and other reserves."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just for the record, we can see that this meeting is recorded as commencing at 9.09 in the morning, and General Mladic's notebook had the time listed as 9.20 in the morning. I'd like to now move on to another example. This is on the second page of the chart. 17 December 1992. And this is 65 ter 22843. If we could have English pages 320 up and B/C/S 297. And I'll start while we're waiting for the English to come up. This is from the 17th of December, 1992. General Mladic's notebook for that day. He's written down that this is for the session of the National Assembly. And if we could now go to page 2 of that document. And I should say for the record, Your Honours, the date appears several pages earlier, but I haven't put all of those into e-court. There's more entries for that day. Could we go to the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. At the starred portion it says "Herceg." Could you just read out what General Mladic's notes were from that entry, just after "Herceg."

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "Our soldiers deliberately fire at transformer station in order to take some oil."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to now, keeping that in mind, please go to P01364. Show page 2 first. Of the English and of the B/C/S. All right. Again we see as in the notebook, 23rd session, with the National Assembly of RS, 17 December 1992. Could we jump now to page 70 of the English and 65 of the B/C/S. All right. Very simply on page 70 of the English we see that Mr. Erceg is speaking. It's written Erceg there, not Herceg as in the diary. And several lines down, Mr. Blaszczyk, can you see a sentence in the middle towards the top of the page. It begins "Electric energy people say ..."?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you just read out this statement, that sentence.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "Electric energy people say that our soldiers are shooting with their" -- it's not clear here, "sterili guns, as the Croats say, at transformer stations for fun and are pleased when oil leaks from such stations."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'd like to now move to the next example where the entries match. This is 19 January, 1993. The top of page 3 of the chart --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 22844 up on the screen, please. Page 76 of the English, 79 of the B/C/S. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And here we have in the middle of the page of General Mladic's notebook "Pale, 19 January 1993. 25th session of the Assembly of the RS." And can you just read out General Mladic's notice number 1 where he is taking notes of what have Mr. Vojislav Maksimovic stated.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: You want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, please, for the record.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Vojislav Maksimovic says here: "We should reject all types of pressure and ultimatums and blackmail. Let's reject the map. Let's negotiate wisely and trust in our strength and weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can look now at that session which is D00115, first page 2 in the B/C/S in English. There we have page 2 up and we see it's the recording of the 25th session of the National Assembly of the RS. Also, it's from the 19th of January. If we could go now to page 15 of the English and also 15 of the B/C/S. And there we see that Mr. Maksimovic is listed as speaking. If we could go to the next page of both the English and B/C/S. And just for the record, if you can see again about the same position on the page, the English, could you read the sentence that begins "That is why we must say decidedly with the utmost ... ," if you could just read out that sentence?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "That is why we must say decidedly and with utmost resolve that we are not afraid and do not accept the dictates of blackmail which have coming out -- our way for some time, now from ruthless Catholic and anti-Orthodox community."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if we could now go to the next page in the English. If we look down the last sentence the paragraph that begins "An in-depth scrutiny of the proposal." If you could read out the sentence that begins "Let us reject that map."

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "Let us reject that map and let us carry on (applause) negotiating as skilfully as we can with our adversaries as well as with our European caretakers and our Yugoslav tutors."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph it's stated: "Let us be wise in negotiations and let us place our faith above all in the strength of our own people and its arms." Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go to the next one now which I'd like to show which is from the 18th of November, 1993. General Mladic's notebook 65 ter 22846, please. While I'm waiting for that to come up in English, again it's 18 November 1993, and it's stated "Geneva." This would be the English, page 35, please. B/C/S page 39. Now, I won't for time read through them all but we can see who are present at these negotiations in Geneva from all sides, and General Mladic, if we go to the next page of his notebook -- well, we can go straight to page 37 of the English, please. All right. And we see there that Ogata has stated: "We have prepared a joint declaration that I hope you will sign today," and a conversation continues. We could go to the next page, please. The next page, please. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. If you could go back. And we see there that it says: "President Karadzic said that General Mladic had several objections item number 3." And below General Mladic has written "My questions." And just for our record, could you read in what his questions are.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "Which materials are at issue? Who are they intended for? How will they be delivered? How and where will they be inspected? Where will delivery be made from?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page now, please. And we see there that General Mladic has written "What items were agreed that Mladic should give his agreement," and then he's written with an arrow next to it, "their response to my questions" about different materials, wood, nails, plastics, clothing, et cetera. Could we go to 65 ter number 21236, a document which matches this meeting, page 1 of both the English and the B/C/S. Well, it's just English that we have up here. And look up at number -- item number 3. Can you just tell us quickly what item number 3 is about, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is allowing UNHCR and ICRS to determine without any conditionality or linkage the content of humanitarian assistance, including needs for all material supplies like gas and other fuel necessary for survival of the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can we go to the next page and look at item number 4. And we see there that it's been included to "ensure that all humanitarian assistance reach its intended civilian beneficiaries and is not diverted to military needs or others." Which addresses some of the concerns we saw in General Mladic's diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we give this 65 ter 21236 a number, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it there should be no objection. Yes, it will be admitted as.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1462, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could go now to the last example I intend to show today. This is from the 25th of August. It's the last item in the chart, beginning -- there were two notebooks which concern this date, 65 ter number 13452 first, please. And, Your Honours, that's the same notebook which we saw on the video and which is here in the courtroom today, the original. And if we could go to page 324 of the English and 328 of the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The transcript should read 13452.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Again, page 24 [sic] of the English, page 328 of the B/C/S. I think the English is not correct. It should be page 324. I think we have the wrong -- that's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Blaszczyk, can you just tell us where this meeting took place on 25th August 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This meeting took place in Dobanovci on 25th August 1995, and here we have listed list of the participants of the meetings, the representative of Yugoslavia and -- and members RS government and army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we just go to the next page, please, in each version. Now, I'm not concerned with the text here other than the last line which states "Continued in next notebook"; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And is this written -- and we can look at the original on the last lined page, the last page which is intended to be written on in this notebook.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Is correct. This entry was written on the last page of this notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And just to be clear again, this notebook is from the 2008 seizure; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This notebook was seized in 4 December 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And is it correct that after this entry there was another entry from September which is, however, written on a cover page, not on a lined page? We can go to the next page maybe and see that.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Is correct. This is another entry written on the cover page from the 5th September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And can we go to the next page of the B/C/S. All right. And what we're seeing there is the final entry from that September meeting on the actual cover page of the notebook; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. If we can now have 65 ter 22851, please, pages 1 to 3 of the English -- starting at page 1 of the English, page 11 of the B/C/S. Now, this notebook we can see is also from Dobanovci, 25th August 1995, and states at the beginning, "Meeting of the Serbian leadership"; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct. The entry is related to the meeting in Dobanovci from 25th August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the first line states "Continued from the previous notebook."

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, it says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the notebook we're looking at now, 65 ter 22851, is from the second seizure in 2010; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct. This notebook was seized on 23 February 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And just for the record, could you read out the first line where General Mladic has put an asterisk next to Karadzic and then written a note what he said?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "Thinks out loud about the role of the USA. Questions --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can stop there for time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to now go to 65 ter 5970, please. Page 1 of both English and B/C/S. Now, this document headed "Record of Meeting of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and Republika Srpska Representatives of the Highest Political and Military Leadership Held on 25 August 1995 in the Army of Yugoslavia Residence in Dobanovci." So this is the same date and place; correct.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct, the same date and the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could we go now to page 6 of the English, page 7 of the B/C/S. And now we saw in the notebook the entry written by General Mladic. Karadzic, "Thinks out loud about the role of the USA." Could you read just the first sentence from the second paragraph of the notes of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "President Karadzic began thinking out loud by saying that America now wants peace but is entirely opposed to war."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "But is not entirely opposed to war," I think is what it says.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: "... is not," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I tender this document, please, Your Honours. This is 65 ter 5970.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This very document, which hasn't been admitted yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1463, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That concludes my direct examination, Your Honour. I'd also like to tender the chart where these five examples appear from which contain another ten similar examples of instances in which General Mladic's notebooks contain notes of a meeting which are corroborated by another document. That chart is 65 ter 22943 again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we not admitted this? Which was the document that we admitted as P1462? Is it a different one? Probably my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that was 21236, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. This chart, 22943 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1464, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I would also seek to tender at this time the corroborating documents listed in this chart which I haven't gone through in the same way with the witness but which he has confirmed that he has reviewed and are accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How many of them are there which hasn't been yet admitted, which is noted only in 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, it should be six of them, Your Honours, and I can read out those numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Robinson, do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Shall we give it -- give them the numbers in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 65 ter 129 will be admitted as.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1465, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the Court Deputy has that chart could you continue to read out all the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think 65 ter 15342 in the second row will come first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I missed it. Thank you. Then that will be admitted as Exhibit P1466. If you could carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then it would be 65 ter number 129 would be the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This has been admitted. 1465.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, then 132.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Will be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1467, Your Honours. 65 ter 6328 will be Exhibit P1468.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1649 will be Exhibit P1469. 65 ter 21236 will be Exhibit P1470.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think 21236 we give a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Oh yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And P1683 will be P1470.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And as far as of the notebooks, Your Honour, I'd propose to deal with that after the cross-examination, the notebooks themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karadzic, it's now for your to cross-examine the witness. Given that this witness gave his direct evidence in live and then Prosecution has spent about -- a bit more than one hour and 30 minutes, and also given the nature of his -- of -- his evidence which is limited to the chain of custody and the authenticity, the Chamber is of the opinion that you should be able to conclude your cross-examination within the same time as the Prosecution has spent, i.e., one hour and half an hour -- one and a half hour. It's now your witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you whether you speak the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I can communicate Serbian language. I wouldn't say that I speak fluently, but I can communicate. I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have in e-court the previous document that we saw, the page of the notebook that we looked at, 5970 is the 65 ter number, and the 65 ter number of the notebook is 22851. It's the same thing that the learned Mr. Nicholls showed on the screen. We'd like to have that as well. Can we have the notebook in the original and the printed version in English. Could we have the English translation in the typewritten version, and on the left part of the screen I'd like to have the original page exhibited. Now on the left side I'd like to ask for the original, please, from this very same notebook. If I'm not clear enough, could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's coming. It will be coming. Probably page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, could I please ask you about what it says after this handwritten part that says "Meeting of the Serbian leadership." If you have a problem with the Cyrillic, I can read it out and you can confirm. Does it say, "Continued from other notebook"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, "Continued from the --" yes, yes. This is written. I cannot translate this word exactly, but "Nastavak iz druge sveske." I don't know how to translate it, but for me it could be both ways in the previous notebook or from the other notebook. But I am not expert in translation at all. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A literal translation would be, do you agree, [In English] "Continuation from another or from the other notebook." [Interpretation] Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: As I said, I'm not interpreter. I am not expert for translation of Serbian language. I can speak and I can communicate but not fluently. I can't say for that one what the translation would be. I think interpreters is in better position to explain this word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not challenging or criticising the meaning of the English translation. It is a translation of the spirit of what it says but not -- it's not a literal translation. I'm saying that because we're going to have quite a few interventions of this kind. Do you agree that the spirit is being conveyed here but not the literal meeting? The previous notebook is right. That's what Mladic meant, but a literal translation would be "The other notebook." Actually, we can ask the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We heard the answer from Mr. Blaszczyk. Please move on. You made the point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us go back a bit. You were in Bosnia-Herzegovina three times; right? In which periods?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Is correct. I was deployed as IPTF officer in 1996, 1998, and 2001, but also very shortly I was in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 2000 -- sorry, in 1992, at the Sarajevo airport, August 1992. But only for two, three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for this period from 1996 to 1998 and 2001, did you deal with or -- did you deal with persons indicted before this Tribunal? Was that part of your work?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did that become part of your work?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Since I joined the ICTY, it was January 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From January 2003 up until the present day, did you deal with my case? Did you work on my indictment and the accompanying material and exhibits and so on?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I was working for so-called Srebrenica case. I was dealing -- I was assigned to the investigation regarding events in Srebrenica from July 1995, what happened exactly during these events and after that, the crimes committed after the liberation or fall of Srebrenica, July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You worked on collecting evidence, evidentiary material, and you worked on contacts with potential witnesses; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct. This is the role of investigator in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were any investigative proceedings started in relation to the treatment of witnesses and the collection of evidentiary material in the Srebrenica case, the case of Popovic et al.?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were any objections raised in respect of you personally and the treatment of witnesses in that case?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I believe -- I think I know what you are talking about, that one of the Defence lawyers from Popovic case put allegation against me that I somehow [indiscernible] the witness from Popovic case, but it wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You're a Pole; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, is correct. I'm Pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you help us understand. In the Polish judiciary system, is there a court investigation involved, or, rather, does the institution of an investigative judge exist?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: No, the system in Poland is entirely different. We have prosecutor, a police, of course, prosecutor office, and a court. Police and prosecutor office conducting an investigation and then the material is submitted to the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know which system we are talking about? Are you familiar with the system in the Yugoslav republics, the system in which an investigative judge exists and when the investigation is actually carried out by that judge?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I know that in Serbia, for example, exists prosecutor, prosecution office, and police, of course, and investigation judge who is conducting the investigation, and this is totally different than in Poland. We have no institution of investigation -- investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you understand then that when in countries, the Balkan countries, a person says "investigator" we understand that to mean a court investigator rather than a prosecution investigator, and do you see any difference involved?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see the relevance of the question. Where are these questions leading us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe you will see that fairly soon because of the way in which evidence is collected and the way in which witnesses are treated in these different systems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put your direct question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are there any legal restrictions in Poland or does the law prescribe how evidence is collected and also how witnesses are called?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ask the question which is related to this material and the investigation conducted by the witness. The situation in Poland has nothing to do with our trial.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the legal regulations in terms of obtaining evidence and treating witnesses in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you do accept that these restrictions and rules exist. Were these rules violated by investigation teams of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the family of General Mladic under pressure that had been initiated from here and carried out by the police in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I am not aware of such situation. I was not involved in any connection with General Mladic wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wife and son. It's not only the wife. Tell us, when was the family home of General Mladic searched for the first time in Belgrade? Before the 4th of December, 2008, were there any other searches?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I remember information that -- I don't know how I got this information. Possible that even from president, but I'm pretty sure that the house was searched on other occasion, but I think it was 2006, but the date exactly I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the explanation you received, if you did receive an explanation, if you asked for one in the first place, namely that the first copies of these notebooks were found only on the 4th of December, 2008.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, we were interested why the material wasn't seized at that time. I mean, the previous search done probably in 2006, but explanation was that at that time they were interested only for looking for ICTY footage of General Mladic. They were not interested of procedure of finding documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: During those previous searches, what was the material that was seized?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I have no information what kind of material was seized during the previous searches, but I think that -- I'm pretty sure that there was one search before 2008, December, but how many more, really, I don't know. For sure ICTY was not involved in these searches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the police in Serbia and in Republika Srpska was guided by directives and pressures coming from this Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I believe this is obligation of Serbian Republika Srpska looking for the fugitives, ICTY fugitives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the search for fugitives. I'm talking about the treatment of families. What is happening to our families down there? Is this some kind of local arbitrary behaviour or is it pressure coming from your services?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Sir, I have no information about this situation. What I read -- what I know only I read in the press, and I know from you, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say, Mr. Blaszczyk, that you don't know that the brother of Osama bin Laden has been treated far better than our children?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We're now going -- I've been very lax in objecting because I thought it would somehow get back to Mr. Blaszczyk's experience, his qualifications, or his knowledge of prior searches, but it is clear that we are now just verging into speeches and nonsense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Agreed. Mr. Karadzic, come back to the relevant questions, to the subject matter dealt with by this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will go back, but I think that I do have the right to test the credibility and the overall behaviour of the witness and the service that he belongs to. However, I will go back to what I had been dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation as to why on the 4th of December all the notebooks had not been seized? Rather, some were seized in February 2010.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: In December 2008, the notebooks seized at that time, the material seized at that time was in the plain view, you know, accessible for everybody. As I know, the material, the notebooks from 2010 search, February 2010 search, was hidden. One in the ward [sic], part of this material was hidden in the attic of Bosiljka Mladic house, and part in the wardrobe in her bedroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the reason why they hadn't been found during the search in 2008?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is the only explanation I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what happened with the material seized during numerous searches of the apartments belonging to my family?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I believe that part of this material was submitted to our evidence units as evidences. I don't know. I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was seized and what happened with the material seized in the homes of many people who are somehow related to me, such as Priest Starovlah, whose house was barged into?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I know that in few searches in Bosnia-Herzegovina, related to you, sir, or your family, there was seized also some documents, and I believe these documents were submitted to the ICTY and are right now are in our evidence unit. But I am not aware of -- I don't know details about these searches, at least from top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are these -- is this material treated as a collection like the material found in the apartment of Mrs. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: What do you mean as a collection? This is evidentiary material, is treated properly, as evidence. Everything what we had received from the people who made the search was submitted, if we received anything, was submitted to us, and then was assigned an ERN number and submit -- and right now in our evidence unit, and, of course, accessible for everybody, including the Defence, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But all this material is kept together. It's not broken down into folders and files. It's kept as a collection of notebooks. And now we also have some audio and video material that we are not going to discuss today. These notebooks are kept as a collection of evidence. Do you have such a collection in my case?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: In fact, this collection from the most recent search of General Mladic was kept somehow differently, but about the collection of the material seized from your residences, I don't know. I know that we have evidences from this search, but I don't know how it is kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now call up in e-court 65 ter 22840?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 98 in both English and Serbian. But in Serbian we need the typewritten text, not the manuscript. Although, if it's the same page, the manuscript will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, Mr. Blaszczyk, is there anyone else who will testify to the authenticity, authenticated the handwriting of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I needed page 98.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether there is anyone else who testified to the authenticity of the handwriting of General Mladic? Except General Manojlo Milovanovic, I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you get the idea to choose General Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: First of all, when he was here in The Hague we took opportunity that he testified. I think it was Stanisic and Simatovic case. And we took this opportunity that he was here in The Hague and we decided to show him this copy or scanned version of General Mladic notebooks. And also having in mind that he was very close to General Mladic entire the war, you know, for many years he attended -- he was attending meetings together with General Mladic. He was present, and he was writing down his notes, and he was very familiar with his handwritings. We decided to choose General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 98 in e-court, not in the document. Page 98 in e-court in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see these first two bullet points? Can you read them for us.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: You mean which one? Which part?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is from a meeting from 16 June 1992, and these are the words of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we perhaps see the previous page to see the beginning of this meeting. Can we go back to the beginning, which is dated 6th June 1992, and then come back to this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a contribution by Karadzic that's written there? And it goes on to straddle the next page, and the date is 6th June 1992. If you accept that this notebook refers to 6th June, 1992, we can go back to the next page to see the text.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I -- I see here English translation and transcript, B/C/S transcript, but I don't see the original notebook, but I believe this is from notebook.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Karadzic says: "We must not exert pressure for people to move," and, "We don't have the right to say that the border is not along the Neretva River"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Is written here, yes. Is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the moving of people is not literally translated? It should not be displacement. The word used in the Serbian is properly translated as "resettlement."

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The same, sir, I think this is not question to me, rather to interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the translation is not the matter this witness is concerned with. You will have another opportunity to challenge the translation or explore the proper translation thereof, but this is not the proper moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this took place at that meeting of the 6 June 1992? If you have the original, you can look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, if you'd like to confirm the date, we can go back to page 93 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I believe if it says so. I believe our case manager is following. Yes, is correct. In the English translation is 6 June, 1992, Hotel Bistrica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see in e-court 1D260. 1D260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you check the number again, Mr. Karadzic. Is it not 1D360?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be 1D260. It's dated 8 June 1992, thus after this meeting it's the reaction and actions of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's in your list as the -- as 1D191. Should we try that document, whether it's the correct document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That could be the document. And this is the document published through the SRNA agency. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't know if we have a translation for this. Can you see that this is dated 8 June 1992? It's an official communique published through the news agency. Do you agree that in line seven it says -- the speaker didn't say who, "... advocates publicly that the basic principles of humanitarian law should be honoured in wartime. The president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic in Bosnia-Herzegovina sends out the following urgent appeal."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. I'm sorry to interrupt. I'm told there is an English translation at D00426, if that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is apparently already admitted. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. If you want me to confirm that this is document dated 8th of June, 1992, from SRNA agency.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just to confirm it has been admitted as Exhibit D426, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that there is a connection between this document published or put out by Karadzic two days after that entry in Mladic's notebook? There is a connection in terms of the subject.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This document was created two days after the meeting which I discussed -- or you discussed just few seconds ago. This is connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this is already an exhibit, can we get 65 ter 22840.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was wondering the line about -- as to your line of questioning. Are you visiting the translation issue again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm sorry to say, Your Excellency, General Mladic's entries in his notebooks are very short, almost shorthand. They are not full, complete sentences, and in translation a lot of misunderstanding can be caused by such shorthand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we'll have a break, Mr. Karadzic, now, for half an hour, but please bear in mind that what we are dealing with today is just simply a chain of custody and the authenticity of the notebook, not the content of the -- content of them. We'll break for half an hour. We resume at 12.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I ask for 65 ter 22852 in e-court. Let's first identify the cover, and then we'll go to page 44 in Serbian and 47 in English. And we need the typewritten text. Serbian typewritten 44. E-court page number 44. Page 47 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Blaszczyk, that it's an entry of the 22nd of March, 1996, when Mladic and his co-workers had a meeting with me?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... conversation with President Karadzic. The date, 22 March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
